newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan car sales rise from strong demand for new models.
newsitem.headline: Japan car sales rise from strong demand for new models.

text.p: Japan's domestic vehicle sales rose in November for the third consecutive month, according to industry figures released on Monday, with gains by industry leader Toyota and good demand for recreational vehicles.
The Japan Automobile Dealers' Association said domestic vehicle sales rose 14 percent in November from a year earlier to 507,548 units, the first double-digit gain in 20 months.
"November's great gain resulted mainly from a sales boost by Toyota," a JADA official said.
He said sales for the whole of 1996 were sure to exceed 5.30 million units and could reach 5.40 million, compared with last year's total of 5.15 million.

Toyota's share of the domestic market, excluding mini-vehicles, rose to 45.2 percent in November, with sales of 229,598 vehicles. That was up from 43.2 percent a year earlier and 43.7 percent in October.
All its new models launched this year -- the Mark II luxury sedan series, and the Ipsum, TownAce Noah and LiteAce Noah minivans -- saw strong demand.
But a Toyota spokesman said the company was not sure if it could maintain the higher market share.

Honda saw continued good news last month with a 47.6 percent jump in sales to 53,497, fuelled by sales of its RVs Step Wagon eight-seater minivan, CR-V light sport-utility vehicle, Odyssey minivan, Orthia station wagon, and S-MX short-body minivan.
Mazda's domestic sales were barely changed at 25,114. It saw strong demand for its Demio compact RV model.
Nissan gained a marginal 0.3 percent in November, partly helped by sales of a low-priced version of its March compact car.
Mitsubishi sales rose 0.2 percent to 38,249, helped by sales of trucks and buses, and Daihatsu sales soared 305.4 percent to 3,677, pushed up by robust sales of its new Pyzar compact minivan.
